analysis.title: LoanDepot Inc. (LDI): Key takeaways from LDI earnings
key_insights: LDI's 3Q26 results missed Street expectations. Lower revenues were partly offset by slightly lower costs. Gain-on-sale (GoS) revenue was below expectations on lower refinance volumes and a lower GoS margin of 3.18% vs 3.40% consensus, partly offset by higher purchase volumes.
Expenses came in slightly below expectations on lower personnel and G&A costs.

4Q26 guidance is weak. Origination volume midpoint is $5.5bn and pull-through weighted lock volume midpoint is $4.25bn, about 17% below consensus. GoS revenue is guided to about $184mn at the midpoint, 22% below the Street.
4Q GoS margin guidance of 3.15-3.55% is higher than 3Q, in part due to a product mix shift towards HELOC loans.
LDI expects 4Q expenses to fall QoQ on lower volume-related costs. It now expects $25mn of annualized savings from productivity initiatives, up from $12mn prior.
LDI expects to reach break-even or profitability by mid-2027 if the mortgage market stays around current levels. It is still running at a net loss.
Shares fell 17% in the session after the results, on the 3Q miss, the softer 4Q outlook and call commentary on the path to profitability and upcoming debt maturities.

Purchase market share is up 9% YoY. The expansion into home equity has scaled LDI into what it believes is a top-three nonbank home equity lender. HELOCs carry smaller average loan balances but higher contribution margins and should reduce reliance on rate-driven refinance activity.
Balance sheet progress: LDI repurchased $87mn of senior notes in 3Q at $0.88 on the dollar and completed about $10bn of MSR sales in 3Q, with another about $9bn through October.

Refinancing upcoming debt maturities remains a key focus. LDI is pursuing several alternatives to refinance or extend the debt and expects to give an update in the near term, with limited detail on the structure.

GS cut its price target to $0.50 from $1.00 and lowered 2026E/2027E/2028E EPS and revenue estimates. It says LDI needs to show a clearer path to profitability and to refinancing its debt before the stock can advance.

market_movers.rationale: GS cut its 12-month target to $0.50 from $1.00, based on a 5.0x 2028E P/E (previously 20.0x on 2027E EPS). Estimates were lowered on a weaker mortgage market and cost growth. Shares were at $0.53 on the 9 Nov 2026 close, implying 5.8% downside.

earnings_insights: LDI 3Q26 reported results missed Street expectations. GoS margin was 3.18% reported vs 3.40% consensus.

4Q26 guidance: origination volume of $4.5-6.5bn ($5.5bn midpoint) and pull-through weighted lock volume of $3.25-5.25bn ($4.25bn midpoint), about 17% below consensus. GoS revenue guided to about $184mn at the midpoint, 22% below consensus.
4Q26 pull-through weighted GoS margin guidance of 3.15-3.55%.
GS revenue estimates (new vs old): 2026E $1,223.8mn vs $1,297.6mn, 2027E $1,265.0mn vs $1,395.5mn, 2028E $1,412.2mn vs $1,503.3mn.
risk_factors: Near-term revenue pressure from lower GoS revenue and softer 4Q volumes.
Refinancing of upcoming debt maturities, with limited detail on structure so far.
Continued net losses, and a mortgage market that must stay around current levels for LDI to reach break-even by mid-2027.
GS-named upside risks: stronger expense leverage and better than anticipated margins.
